### Problem

The issue schema check reads any comment closer (two dashes and a greater-than sign) or comment opener (a less-than sign, an exclamation mark and two dashes) inside a PRD or Spec section as an HTML comment, even inside inline code or a fenced code block, and fails G1 with "has an HTML comment; nothing in the PRD or Spec may be hidden from the person who reads it". In DiluxOne/diluxone-mermaid that closer is Mermaid's edge syntax (an arrow from A to B is written as A, two dashes, a greater-than sign, B), so any issue that quotes a diagram is refused although nothing is hidden: https://github.com/DiluxOne/diluxone-mermaid/issues/15 (a reproduced bug) sat 10 days in `needs-human` because its Spec quoted an edge from `A` to `end` in backticks, and the autopilot does not start on it either. The test is in `check()` in `scripts/issue-schema.py` (it tests whether the section text contains the opener or the closer anywhere).

### Scope

- An HTML comment is found only where it would be hidden: outside inline code spans and fenced code blocks. A real HTML comment in the text still fails the check.
- The same rule holds wherever the engine looks for hidden comments in a PRD or Spec (the check, G1, and the shape check of an edit).

### Out of scope

- The engine's own markers before an issue's first section.
- Which sections must be present.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given a Spec section that quotes a Mermaid edge from `A` to `B` in inline code or in a fenced code block, when the schema check runs, then it passes.
- C2: Given a PRD or Spec section with a real HTML comment outside code, when the schema check runs, then it fails with the same message as today.
- C3: Given a lone comment closer in plain text outside code, when the schema check runs, then it fails as today.

### Criticality

Normal
